message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I would not call this ECG normal.** From the image, the rhythm is regular at roughly 105–110 beats/minute, but there is **ST-segment elevation in the front chest leads, especially V2–V4**, with abnormal R-wave progression.

These changes can indicate a heart attack, although other conditions or previous heart damage can produce similar appearances. A photo alone cannot reliably distinguish them; this needs clinician assessment, comparison with previous ECGs, and potentially repeat ECGs and troponin blood tests.

**If you have chest discomfort, breathlessness, sweating, nausea, or faintness now, call your local emergency number immediately and don’t drive yourself.** [American Heart Association guidance](https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/heart-attack/warning-signs-of-a-heart-attack). If this ECG was just taken, have the treating clinician review it immediately, even without symptoms.

When was it recorded, and were you having any symptoms?
